profilePeriod: Premiership, 1969–1974, informed by earlier labour and foreign-ministry service.

sources.title: Golda Meir: Knesset biography
sources.evidence: Labour minister promoted immigrant housing and public employment; prime minister led parliamentary coalitions from 1969, faced criticism over poverty and the 1973 war. Search-index text available; direct open returned no readable text.

sources.title: Golda Meir, Minister of Labour, 1954
sources.evidence: Primary photograph documents her presenting the first maternity grant. Catalogue describes National Insurance Law, housing and infrastructure programmes.

sources.title: For the Attainment of Peace: Golda Meir speech
sources.evidence: Meir advocates defensible borders, arms supply and foreign assistance alongside negotiated peace and open trade. She calls for taxes, compulsory loans and curbed consumption while improving lower-income conditions and absorbing immigrants.

sources.title: Statement to Knesset by Prime Minister Meir
sources.evidence: She seeks parliamentary confidence after December 1973 elections; defends Egyptian disengagement, Geneva negotiations and military deterrence, rejects return to June 1967 lines. Search-index full document retrieved; direct page fetch returned 403.

sources.title: Golda Meir interview on peace and religion
sources.evidence: Direct interview: rejects defining Israel as a religious state, values Judaism as historical national bond, acknowledges religious marriage difficulties but favours patient compromise. Discusses education aid related to family income.

sources.title: Meir plea for secular-religious coexistence
sources.evidence: Contemporary speech report: urges coexistence, opposes exclusion from Jewish community and warns against simplistic resolutions of religious disputes.

sources.title: EEC-Israel preferential trade treaty
sources.evidence: Contemporary account of treaty signed by her foreign minister: reciprocal but asymmetric tariff reductions, larger European reductions for Israeli exports than Israeli concessions on imports.

sources.title: MASHAV history, Israeli embassy Cameroon
sources.evidence: Official account attributes MASHAV creation to Meir after African visit: knowledge exchange and agricultural self-sufficiency for new states in hot, semi-arid climates.

sources.title: Oriana Fallaci interview with Golda Meir
sources.evidence: Reproduced direct interview: she values motherhood and marriage, sharply rejects radical liberation movement, yet defends her lifelong political work among men. Describes commitment to communal kibbutz life. Translation/reproduction is not original magazine facsimile.

sources.title: US Special Actions Group meeting minutes
sources.evidence: Contemporary US official record confirms Meir told ambassador Israel would not launch a preemptive attack despite imminent hostilities.

sources.title: Israeli enquiry: Koppel Committee
sources.evidence: Meir proposed judicial inquiry into Munich security failures; cabinet majority rejected it. She appointed inquiry team; report sought improved security abroad. Evidence of both intelligence priorities and constrained accountability, not unchecked personal rule.

sources.title: My Life, publisher catalogue
sources.evidence: Publisher credits Golda Meir and describes political autobiography covering Zionism, socialism, state creation and premiership; qualifies as political memoir.

sources.title: My Life, first American edition catalogue
sources.evidence: Catalogue identifies Golda Meir, Putnam, 1975, and distinguishes editions. Work first published 1975.

sources.title: Minha Vida, Brazilian edition catalogue
sources.evidence: Bookseller identifies Minha Vida by Golda Meir, Bloch Editores, 1976. Modern ISBN in listing is inconsistent, so only title/publisher/year of described physical edition used; corroborated by Brazilian Morasha bibliography.

sources.title: Morasha bibliography
sources.evidence: Brazilian bibliography explicitly cites Meir, Golda, Minha Vida, Bloch Editores 1976, Brasil.

sources.title: My Life original copyright page reproduction
sources.evidence: Extract reproduces copyright Golda Meir 1975 and first Great Britain publication by Weidenfeld & Nicolson in 1975. Resolves erroneous 1973/1974 web dates; A Land of Our Own is a distinct compilation.

sources.title: Israel economic report
sources.evidence: World Bank account records broad price controls 1970–1972, followed by controls on fourteen basic items, and use of budget restraint to fight inflation.

facts: National immigrant housing, social insurance and public works exemplify central direction (1949–1956).
Prime minister conducts nationwide coalition programme and national defence in 1969–1974.
estrutura.tension: Unitary state-building does not abolish local institutions or cooperative autonomy; detailed federal propositions are analogical, not recorded Meir proposals.

facts: Sought Knesset confidence after December 1973 elections.
In September 1972 requested judicial security inquiry but was outvoted in cabinet.
representacao.tension: Party-led parliamentary democracy rather than direct-democracy assemblies; occupied noncitizens lacked the democratic rights of Israeli citizens.

facts: Security inquiry and recommendations strengthened protection abroad after Munich.
War and terrorism were major governmental priorities while parliamentary opposition survived.
poder.tension: Strong security state does not imply death penalty for ordinary crime or suppression of all offensive dissent.

facts: Labour ministry organised immigrant housing and employment; 1970 speech makes immigrant absorption a national economic priority.
1971 speech opposes excluding people from Jewish community.
imigracao.tension: Mass Jewish immigration and cultural diversity within Jewry coexist with a Jewish national identity; this is not universal open borders.

facts: 1974 statement couples deterrence with disengagement and negotiated peace.
Refused preemptive strike on October 6, 1973.
diplomacia.tension: Rejects both disarmament and war as an end in itself; preemption is conditional and constrained by allies.

facts: 1970 speech asserts border defence against hostile forces and seeks international backing.
1974 negotiations defend strategic borders but accept separation of forces.
intervencao.tension: Assertive regional security and diplomatic assistance abroad coexist with reluctance toward unlimited conquest.

facts: Labour ministry built housing and national insurance, including maternity support.
1970 speech promises advancement of lower incomes during emergency austerity.
economia.tension: Cooperative and public provision coexist with private firms; no evidence for blanket abolition of property or violent economic revolution.

facts: 1970 speech calls for taxes, compulsory loans and national coordination of consumption, wages and productivity.
Controls on prices operated broadly 1970–1972 and continued on basic goods in 1973.
controle.tension: Pragmatic mixed economy and emergency restraint, not total command economy or perpetual deficit expansion.

facts: 1970 EEC treaty lowered tariffs reciprocally while preserving asymmetric protection.
1970 speech stresses both essential imports and curbing external deficits.
comercio.tension: Supports export markets and strategic domestic capacity; neither autarky nor tariff-free global market.

facts: 1971 interview rejects religious-state definition while cherishing Judaism as historical bond.
Marriage arrangements retained alongside pleas for secular-religious coexistence.
religiao.tension: Secular political reasoning combined with institutional religious accommodation; neither theocracy nor militant eradication of faith.

facts: 1954 maternity grants support working mothers.
1972 interview values family and childbirth but rejects restricting herself to domestic life.
moral.tension: Economic equality for women does not establish modern LGBT, gender-language or sexual-liberation positions. These require cautious analogy.

facts: MASHAV established under Meir to exchange practical agricultural and development expertise.
National public infrastructure and technical development accompany personal attachment to kibbutz life.
tecnologia.tension: Productive science and rural cooperative life coexist; modern human enhancement and AI are hypothetical, with weaker confidence than infrastructure.

limitations: Historical model fixed at Premiership, 1969–1974, informed by earlier labour and foreign-ministry service. No later private positions used.

Brazil-specific institutions are translated into comparable Israeli policy choices; digital policing, AI, embryo editing and current identity questions are explicit value-based extrapolations, not quotations.
No source establishes a personal view on every modern item. Ambivalence is used only where documented principles conflict, not as a substitute for research.
Some official pages were accessible through search-index text only. Direct interview reproductions have provenance limitations recorded above.

Book date conflicts found in tertiary pages; first-edition catalogue and original copyright-page reproduction support 1975. Book serves recommendation only and does not expand historical answer period.

recommendedMetadata.reason: PT and EN accurately describe premiership, labour welfare legacy, Jewish immigration, security, religious compromise and disengagement. Coordinator notified before answering.

bookDecision.reason: Self-authored political memoir, more relevant and widely known than collected speeches. No existing books.json entry. Author Golda Meir; Brazilian title verified separately; first publication 1975.

processNotes.independence: Read no answer archive, stored vector, score report, similarity review or other profile answers. Existing research consulted only for profilePeriod and source URLs. One independent audit; no further delegation.
likelyNeighboursAndDistinctions: David Ben-Gurion: common labour-Zionist state-building background; Meir model focuses on her social-insurance legacy, 1970 ceasefire and post-1973 disengagement decisions.
Menachem Begin: common insistence on Israeli security and Jewish immigration; Meir retained labour/cooperative economics and accepted initiatives opposed by Gahal/Likud in 1970–1974.
Yitzhak Rabin: common Labour and security context; do not import later Oslo positions into Meir’s 1969–1974 model.
Labour Zionism and social democracy are conceptual neighbours; her religious compromise, selective immigration and regional conflict must remain explicit.

archetypeReasoning.sociedade: D: egalitarian labour and civil institutions best fit the offered options, qualified by Jewish national boundaries and conservative family attitudes.
archetypeReasoning.economia: B: cooperative institutions, welfare and regulation.
archetypeReasoning.mundo: B: strong defence and close allies alongside negotiated disengagement.
archetypeReasoning.tecnologia: D: productive technical development without unrestricted enhancement.
